sentences.text:
This appeal is filed under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (in short 'the M.V. Act') against the decree and award dated 19.09.2005 in the M.V.O.P No.36 of 2004 on the file of Chairman,
Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal -cum- I Additional District Judge, Kurnool, awarding compensation of Rs.2,63,400/- with costs and interest at the rate of 7.5% p.a from the date of petition till the date of deposit with joint and several liability of the respondents No.1 and 2.
2.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The case of the claimants, in briefly, is as follows:
The petitioner No.1 is the wife and the petitioners No.2 to 5 are the children of The New India Assurance Co Ltd Rep.

By ... vs Smt V. Ramakka 4 Others on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166318344/
1 V.Chettappa, (the deceased) who was doing watch business and earning Rs.5000/-
p.m.
The deceased was aged 30 years.
On 14.09.2003, at 6.00 A.M., he boarded a R.T.C. bus bearing No. AP 10 Z 1745 at Sathupalli Village, Khammam District to go to Chaparalapalli Village, Khammam District.

On the way, when the bus reached near Gayatri office, within the outskirts of Sathupalli village, a lorry bearing No.AP 31 W 8555, coming in the opposite direction being driven in a rash and negligent manner with high speed, dashed the bus.
As a result, the deceased was thrown out of the window and fell on the ground and the lorry ran over him resulting in grievous injuries to him.
Later, the injured was taken to the government hospital for treatment.
He succumbed to the injuries.
The case in Crime No.137 of 2003 was registered by the S.H.O. of Sathupalli Police Station.
3. The respondent No.1 who is the owner of the lorry remained ex parte.
The respondent No.2 which is the insurer of the lorry filed counter opposing the claim.
The respondent No.3 who is the owner of the bus filed separate counter opposing the claim.
4. The petitioner No.1 was examined as PW1 and J.Annamaiah was examined as PW2 and Exs.A1 to A5 were marked,

which reads as follows:
Ex.A1 - Certified copy of F.I.R.
Ex.
A2 - Certified copy of inquest report.
Ex.A3 - Certified copy of post mortem report.

Ex.A4 - Certified copy of M.V.I. report.
Ex.A5 - Certified copy of charge sheet.
On behalf of the respondent No.3, the driver of A.P.S.R.T.C., was examined as RW1 but no document was marked.

Further, on behalf of the respondent No.2, a copy of policy of the insurance was marked as Ex.B1 and a photostat letter addressed to S.H.O., Sathupalli Police Station by RW1, dated 14.09.2003 was marked as Ex. B2.
5.
After hearing both the parties, the Tribunal held that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of the lorry only.

The Tribunal assessed notional income of the decease at Rs.1800/- per month out of which 1/3rd was deducted towards personal expenditure and the remaining amount was multiplied by 12, which equals to Rs.14,400/-, was taken as his annual contribution to the family.
By adopting multiplier '16' from the schedule-II under the M.V. Act, the Tribunal granted compensation of Rs.2,30,400/-.

In addition there to, Rs.15,000/- was granted towards loss of consortium to the wife and another amount of Rs.15,000/- was granted towards the loss of estate, Rs.2500/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.500/- towards transportation of the dead body.
Thus, the Tribunal awarded Rs.2,63,400/- with costs and interest as aforesaid.

sentences.text: Aggrieved by the award and decree passed, this appeal was preferred contending that the amount awarded is high and the rate of interest is also high.

It is further contended that sections 166 and 163 A of the M.V. Act, are inconsistent and the claim under both provisions simultaneously is not maintainable as held by the Apex Court in the case of Deepal Girishbhai Soni and Others Vs.

entities.text: Deepal Girishbhai Soni and Others Vs.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: United
India Insurance Co.Ltd1
. It is also contended that as per the schedule-II of the M.V. Act, the amount of income shall be treated as Rs.1,250/- but not Rs.1,800/-, which had no basis.
It is also contended that the narration of the accident that the deceased has been thrown out from the window of the bus and fallen on the ground and run over by the lorry is highly impossible.
Since no eye witness was examined, the alleged rash and negligence was not proved.
It is mandatory to prove the same by examining any eye witness.
7. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant.
He reiterated the grounds of the appeal.

8. Merely because the claimants mentioned sections 166 and 163 A of the M.V. Act, when the claimants establish rashness or negligence of the driver of the crime vehicle in causing the accident,
unless the claim is limited to section 163 A of the M.V. Act, the schedule-II need not be followed.
Therefore, the contentions that the claim cannot be entertained under both the provisions and that the notional income of the deceased shall be taken as Rs.1,250/- are not acceptable.

Therefore,
deciding the award under fault liability under section 166 of the M.V. Act and the amount of notional income of the deceased as taken by the Tribunal needs no interference.
(2004) 5 SCC 385 9. Insofar as, the rate of interest is concerned, as it is just and reasonable as, in the year 2003, it is not at all high and the same does not require interference.
10. Insofar as, the rash and negligence is concerned, though no eye witness was examined, the manner of the accident itself speaks the negligence as decided by the Tribunal.
11. As such, there is no merit in the appeal.
12. In the result, the Motor Accident Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is dismissed without costs.
Interim orders granted earlier, if any, shall stand vacated.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
